correctness.rationale: Every vertex is a generic-support maximizer; for each positive leaf rank j the coefficient counts subsets by binomial(r-j,h-1). The nonnegative vertex coordinates imply the exact squared-distance upper bound T²+sum(a_j²)-2y(T-y). Equality forces one endpoint at the hub apex and the other at full leaf support, because r>=2 and w1>0. Distinctness follows from Pascal difference identities. The proof has all quantifiers and covers arbitrary admissible real weights; 30 exhaustive rational small cases and 299 binomial instances corroborate.

originality.rationale: Pešović–Stojadinović (2022, arXiv:2209.12053v1) defines and enumerates m-graph polytopes but does not evaluate the Euclidean diameters or classify diametral pairs. Behrend (2024, arXiv:2403.06975v1) and Behrend et al. (arXiv:2207.14253v3) analyze partial permutohedra and their simplex sums. A known leaf-coordinate partial-permutohedron diameter does not imply the lifted hub-coordinate Euclidean diameter because of the additional rank-one squared coordinate-sum term. Explicit searches did not uncover the full weighted formula, though stronger unnamed sources remain possible.

value.rationale: The m-graph interpolation on a star is a canonical family between the graphical zonotope and graph associahedron. The theorem computes its exact natural Euclidean diameter and every diametral pair in all dimensions, for the entire meaningful nonnegative cardinality-weighted cone, and locates a sharp change from one to r! maximizing pairs. The full ambient metric matters intrinsically and differs from a known projected metric; this is more structural than a reparameterized number or arbitrary finite sample.
